look_here_first: Start with the lower leaf surface and fruit bloom. Berlandier/Heller's grape has a lower leaf surface that remains visible—sparsely webby/hairy to nearly glabrous—not a solid white felt. Branchlets are slightly angled and usually lack red-banded nodes; ripe berries are conspicuously glaucous and the fruiting clusters are comparatively short and compact.

lookalikes.differences: Vitis mustangensis: Mustang grape has dense white/rust wool completely concealing the leaf underside and larger, less-glaucous berries. Vitis cinerea: Current/FNA var. cinerea has distinctly angled branchlets densely hirtellous plus arachnoid, more consistently hairy lower leaf surfaces and only slightly glaucous berries; in Texas it is primarily eastern. Vitis palmata: V. palmata has uniformly red/purple branchlets and usually deeply 3–5-lobed glabrous leaves.
